test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first one walks at 12.6 km/hr. The other one walks at 27 km/hr. The train takes 12.5 and 14 seconds, respectively, to overtake them. What is the speed of the train if both the persons are walking in the same direction as the train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **same direction**, (ST − S₁) × T₁ = (ST − S₂) × T₂ = **Length of Train**.

(ST − 12.6) × 12.5 = (ST − 27) × 14

12.5ST − 157.5 = 14ST − 378

1.5ST = 220.5 ⇒ ST = 220.5 ÷ 1.5 = 147 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 147 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/427b1d5173fa18e13287ec5a4e99a42e7ea1265dd5541fb224ee8ea5033ab0f6.png] 

**Given:** Speed of **Person 1** (S₁) = 12.6 km/hr, Time 1 (T₁) = 12.5 s

**Given:** Speed of **Person 2** (S₂) = 27 km/hr, Time 2 (T₂) = 14 s

**Formula:** Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Let **Train Speed** be S km/hr.

⇒ Length L = (S − 12.6) × (5/18) × 12.5 --- (i)

⇒ Length L = (S − 27) × (5/18) × 14 --- (ii)

⇒ (S − 12.6) × 12.5 = (S − 27) × 14

⇒ 12.5S − 157.5 = 14S − 378

⇒ 14S − 12.5S = 378 − 157.5

⇒ 1.5S = 220.5

⇒ S = 220.5 ÷ 1.5 = 147 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 147 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When moving in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (u − v). When moving in **opposite directions**, it is the sum (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train Overtaking a Moving Object

Length of Train = (Relative Speed) × (Time taken to cross). This formula assumes the length of the person/point object is negligible.</p
